summary: Little White Mountain lookout above Kelowna: in use by 1913, improved in 1924, and burned by vandals in the winter of 2005-06.

facts.status_note: Vandals burned the old Ministry of Forests lookout tower in the winter of 2005-06, per a 2006 volunteer newsletter. No source describes what remains.
facts.agency: Forest Branch, Department of Lands (1921 and 1924 reports); Ministry of Forests (tower in 2006)

access.note: The 2006 newsletter says BC Parks took out part of Little White Road to keep motor traffic out and built a footpath for permitted uses. No source describes access today.

visit.trail_note: The Crawford Trail, which the 2006 newsletter says extends almost 20 km, runs to the top of Little White Mtn., mostly through Myra-Bellevue Provincial Park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief names the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary. The sources place the mountain near Kelowna, in the central Okanagan Valley, not in the Kootenay Boundary area. The story does not name a regional district. The editor should confirm the correct unit.

notes_for_editor: The 1913 to 1924 entries come from Canada Lookouts summaries of Forest Branch reports and a 1913 newspaper item. The archive gives no build date, staffing or description of the tower, so the story has none. The 2005-06 burning comes from a single 2006 volunteer newsletter, which says 'last winter' and does not give the date of the fire itself. The brief local_unit Regional District of Kootenay Boundary looks wrong: the mountain is near Kelowna, and the brief's coordinates (49.699, -119.332) sit south-east of Kelowna. I did not find a source that names the correct regional district, so no correction is proposed. The brief access unknown is replaced by restricted, which rests on 2006 information only. No photo was added. The Wikipedia page is used for elevation and location only.
